title: Centre launches Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign in fresh push to tourism
excerpt: Union Minister of Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and National Mission for Alternative Destinations-Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign on World Tourism Day 2026.New Delhi, Sep 27 (IANS) Union Minister of Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and National Mission for Alternative Destinations—Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign on World Tourism Day 2026.The Ministry also exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with industry partners for joint tourism promotion and marketing.Addressing the event at Bharat Mandapam here, the minister said, "The next phase of India's tourism journey must ensure that growth reaches beyond popular destinations, creating opportunities for local communities, entrepreneurs, women and youth while making tourism more balanced, inclusive and sustainable.""Tourism is no longer just about visiting places; today's travellers seek authentic experiences—local cuisine, local art, local traditions and meaningful connections that create memories, not merely photographs," he observed.Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0 seeks to distribute tourism demand more widely by promoting tourism-ready, lesser-known destinations as alternatives or complements to destinations experiencing heavy tourist footfall. In collaboration with States and Union Territories, the initiative will identify destinations with a distinct appeal, adequate infrastructure and accommodation, and the capacity to receive additional visitors sustainably. The initial focus will be on hill and mountain destinations, coastal and waterfront destinations, heritage and cultural towns, and regional pilgrimage destinations.On the occasion, the Ministry of Tourism exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Airbnb India Private Limited, FlixBus India Private Limited, Glance Digital Experience Private Limited (InMobi Group), Eicher Group Foundation and MakeMyTrip (India) Limited to strengthen destination promotion, community participation and responsible tourism.The National Digital Tourism Stack, being developed in collaboration with ONDC and with the support of the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), aims to make India's tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy. This shared digital infrastructure will enable tourism providers to make their offerings available across participating platforms, supported by capabilities such as verified identities and supplier credentials, search and discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal. Envisaged as a collaborative effort involving the Ministry, States, Union Territories and industry, the programme will be implemented in phases with a pilot planned for January 2027.Delivering the welcome address, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Bhuvnesh Kumar said, "Artificial Intelligence, digital platforms and data-driven destination management can make tourism more accessible, responsive and personalised. India has considerable experience in Digital Public Infrastructure, and we are now looking at how these capabilities can be brought together for tourism."Vivek Raghavan, co-Founder, Sarvam AI, delivered the keynote address on this year's World Tourism Day theme, "Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism." He stated that AI has the potential to transform every stage of the tourism journey — from discovering destinations and planning a trip to booking, experiencing and sharing it. The opportunity before us is to use technology to make travel more seamless, personalised and accessible, while creating a customised experience for every traveller."

title: Centre launches Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign in fresh push to tourism
excerpt: Digital Desk | New Delhi, Sep 27 (IANS) Union Minister of Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday launched the National Digital Tourism Stack and National Mission for Alternative Destinations—Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 campaign on World Tourism Day 2026. The Ministry also exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with industry partners for joint tourism promotion and marketing. Addressing the event at Bharat Mandapam here, the minister said, “The next phase of India’s tourism journey must ensure that growth reaches beyond popular destinations, creating opportunities for local communities, entrepreneurs, women and youth while making tourism more balanced, inclusive and sustainable.” “Tourism is no longer just about visiting places; today’s travellers seek authentic experiences—local cuisine, local art, local traditions and meaningful connections that create memories, not merely photographs,” he observed. Dekho Apna Desh Campaign 2.0 seeks to distribute tourism demand more widely by promoting tourism-ready, lesser-known destinations as alternatives or complements to destinations experiencing heavy tourist footfall. In collaboration with States and Union Territories, the initiative will identify destinations with a distinct appeal, adequate infrastructure and accommodation, and the capacity to receive additional visitors sustainably. The initial focus will be on hill and mountain destinations, coastal and waterfront destinations, heritage and cultural towns, and regional pilgrimage destinations. On the occasion, the Ministry of Tourism exchanged five Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with Airbnb India Private Limited, FlixBus India Private Limited, Glance Digital Experience Private Limited (InMobi Group), Eicher Group Foundation and MakeMyTrip (India) Limited to strengthen destination promotion, community participation and responsible tourism. The National Digital Tourism Stack, being developed in collaboration with ONDC and with the support of the International Centre for DPI Innovation and Advancement (ICDIA), aims to make India’s tourism offerings more discoverable, accessible and trustworthy. This shared digital infrastructure will enable tourism providers to make their offerings available across participating platforms, supported by capabilities such as verified identities and supplier credentials, search and discovery, payments, ratings and grievance redressal. Envisaged as a collaborative effort involving the Ministry, States, Union Territories and industry, the programme will be implemented in phases with a pilot planned for January 2027. Delivering the welcome address, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Bhuvnesh Kumar said, “Artificial Intelligence, digital platforms and data-driven destination management can make tourism more accessible, responsive and personalised. India has considerable experience in Digital Public Infrastructure, and we are now looking at how these capabilities can be brought together for tourism.” Vivek Raghavan, co-Founder, Sarvam AI, delivered the keynote address on this year’s World Tourism Day theme, “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism.” He stated that AI has the potential to transform every stage of the tourism journey — from discovering destinations and planning a trip to booking, experiencing and sharing it. The opportunity before us is to use technology to make travel more seamless, personalised and accessible, while creating a customised experience for every traveller."

title: વાવાઝોડાના હચમચાવી મૂકે તેવા CCTV
excerpt: વાવાઝોડાના ભયાનકતા CCTV કેમેરામાં કેદ થઈ છે. આ દ્રશ્યો બિહારના વૈશાલી જિલ્લાના છે, જ્યાં મોડી સાંજે વાતાવરણમાં અચાનક પલટો જોવા મળ્યા બાદ ભારે વંટોળની સ્થિતિ જોવા મળી હતી. આ વંટોળ એટલો ભયાનક હતો કે લોકોના મકાનના છાપડા ઉડાડી દીધા હતા. એટલું જ નહીં અન્ય સાધન સામગ્રીને પણ ઉડાડી અને એક મહાકાય વૃક્ષને મૂળમાંથી ઉખાડી ફેંક્યું હતું. મહત્વનું છે કે છેલ્લા કેટલાક દિવસથી આ વિસ્તારમાં મોસમનો બદલાયેલો મિજાજ જોવા મળી રહ્યો છે, ક્યારે ભારે તો ક્યારેક સામાન્ય પવન ફૂંકાતા જનજીવન અસ્તવ્યસ્ત બન્યું છે. સૌથી વધુ કપરી સ્થિતિ શેરપુર માનિકપુર પંચાયતની છે. જ્યા 8-9 ડઝન મકાનના શેડ ઉડી જવાની અને ઝાડ ધરાશાયી થવાની ઘટના બની છે.

title: ધારાસભ્યની દોડતી કારનું ટાયર ફાટ્યું !
excerpt: પૂરપાટ ઝડપે કાર હાઈવે પરથી પસાર થઈ રહી હોય અને ટાયર ફાટે તો કેવું થાય? આ સવાલનો જવાબ આપતી ઘટના CCTV કેમેરામાં કેદ થઈ છે. ઉત્તરપ્રદેશના બુલંદશહેરના ગંગા એક્સપ્રેસ પરથી પસાર થતી એક ફોર્ચ્યૂનર કારને અકસ્માત નડ્યો. વરસાદી માહોલ વચ્ચેથી જ્યારે આ મોંઘીદાટ કાર પૂરપાટ ઝડપી પસાર થઈ રહી હતી, ત્યારે અચાનક તેનું ટાયર ફાટે છે અને કાર બેકાબૂ બનીને રસ્તાના કિનારે રહેલ એક થાંભલા સાથે ટકરાય છે. નવાઈની બાબત એ છે કે આ કાર ડિબાઈના ધારાસભ્ય ચંદ્રપાલસિંહ લોધીની કાર હતી અને તેઓ ખુદ આ કારમાં સવાર હતા. જો કે બનાવ અંગેની જાણ થતાં જ પોલીસ ઘટના સ્થળે પહોંચી અને રેસ્ક્યૂ કર્યું હતું. પ્રાથમિક જાણકારી પ્રમાણે નેતાજી સહિત 2 લોકો ઈજાગ્રસ્ત થયાં છે. ધારાસભ્ય જ્યારે લખનૌથી ગાઝિયાબાદ પરત જઈ રહ્યા હતા ત્યારે આ દુર્ઘટના સર્જાઈ હતી.

title: The Tech-led Renaissance: Space, semiconductors and AI in PM Narendra Modi’s India
excerpt: The geopolitical and economic landscape of the twenty-first century is defined not merely by military might or geographical size, but by technological sovereignty. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India has transitioned from a passive consumer of global technologies into an active creator, innovator, and exporter of frontier tech. This article explores the structural, policy and scientific transformations that have reshaped India’s technology ecosystem since 2014. By focusing on three strategic pillars—Space, Semiconductors and Artificial Intelligence—we examine how the Indian state has leveraged technology to drive domestic development, ensure national security and project power on the global stage. The New Space Age: Democratization and deep space India’s space program, long recognized for its frugality and efficiency under the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), underwent a structural mutation under the Modi administration. The shift was clear move from a state-monopolized sector to a thriving commercial space ecosystem. The Policy Pivot: IN-SPACe and the Space Policy 2023 For decades, private players in India could only act as vendors supplying components to ISRO. The establishment of the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) in 2020 completely altered this dynamics . By acting as a single-window autonomous clearance agency, IN-SPACe allowed private companies to build rockets, launch satellites, and utilize ISRO’s world-class infrastructure. The formalization of the Indian Space Policy 2023 codified this openness, providing regulatory clarity that attracted substantial venture capital into aerospace startups like Skyroot Aerospace and Agnikul Cosmos. Historical Milestones: Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan and Aditya-L1 The geopolitical prestige of India’s space program reached its zenith with the Chandrayaan-3 mission. By successfully landing the Vikram lander on the lunar South Pole—a region untouched by any other spacefaring nation—India demonstrated immaculate engineering precision under extreme constraints. This followed the success of the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) and paved the way for Aditya-L1, India’s first dedicated solar observatory. These missions proved that India could execute deep-space exploration at a fraction of the cost incurred by Western counterparts. Commercialization and global launches Through New Space India Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of ISRO, India positioned itself as a highly reliable, cost-effective launch hub for global payloads. The deployment of massive satellite constellations, such as the UK-based One Web fleet using India’s heaviest rocket, the LVM3, solidified India’s market share in the global launch services sector, turning space technology into a vital driver of foreign exchange and diplomatic soft power. The Silicon Shield: Establishing the semiconductor ecosystem If space represents India’s external ambitions, semiconductors represent the foundational hardware upon which its digital economy rests. Recognizing the vulnerability of global supply chains during the pandemic, the Modi government launched an aggressive campaign to bring silicon fabrication to Indian soil. The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) Launched with a massive financial outlay of ₹76,000 crore (approximately $10 billion), the India Semiconductor Mission was designed to position India as a global hub for electronics manufacturing and design. Unlike previous, short-lived government attempts, the ISM offered comprehensive 50% fiscal support for the setting up of semiconductor fabs, display fabs, and compound semiconductor facilities. Megaprojects and infrastructure The policy yielded tangible results with the approval of massive semiconductor units across the country. Partnerships between domestic giants like the Tata Group and international firms (such as Taiwan’s PSMC and Japan’s Renesas) led to the establishment of India’s first commercial semiconductor fabs in Dholera, Gujarat, and assembly and test facilities in Sanand and Morigaon, Assam. Simultaneously, US chip giant Micron Technology commenced construction on a major Assembly, Testing, Marking, and Packaging (ATMP) facility, integrating India directly into the global microchip supply chain. Design and human capital While fabrication plants require years to mature, India already possessed a massive competitive advantage: design talent. Nearly 20% of the world’s semiconductor design engineers are located in India, working out of R&D hubs in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune. The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme targeted local startups, encouraging them to design domestic chips (IP core creation) for local consumption and export, ensuring that India moves up the value chain from basic assembly to high-end design ownership. Artificial Intelligence: Sovereignty, scale and social good The PM Modi government’s approach to Artificial Intelligence differs distinctively from the purely commercial model of Silicon Valley and the state-controlled model of Beijing. India’s AI philosophy is anchored in the principle of “AI for All”—using machine learning to solve large-scale socio-economic challenges at the grassroots level. Also Read: Major Deepwater Gas Discovery: ONGC strikes gas in Mahanadi Basin off Odisha under Samudra Manthan Campaign The India AI Mission With a cabinet approval of over ₹10,371 crore, the India AI Mission established a sovereign framework for AI development. The cornerstone of this initiative is the creation of a massive, public-tier AI computing infrastructure. By making thousands of advanced GPUs available to local startups, researchers, and public enterprises, the government aims to eliminate the high financial barriers to AI model training. Foundational models and linguistic diversity India’s unparalleled linguistic diversity presents a unique challenge for standard Western LLMs. Under the Bhashini initiative, the government deployed AI to break language barriers in real-time. Bhashini uses open-source datasets to train models capable of translating Indian languages dynamically, allowing rural citizens to access government services, digital banking, and legal documents in their native dialects. Furthermore, public-private partnerships have fueled the creation of indigenous LLMs, such as Krutrim and Hanooman, designed specifically to understand the cultural nuances and syntax of the Indian population. AI in public governance AI has been deeply integrated into India’s public infrastructure. In agriculture, predictive AI models analyze weather patterns, soil health, and crop pricing to provide actionable insights directly to farmers via mobile devices. In healthcare, AI-powered diagnostic tools are deployed in Ayushman Bharat health centers to screen for conditions like diabetic retinopathy and tuberculosis in remote villages where specialized doctors are unavailable. The Convergence: DPI, security and geopolitics The true power of India’s technological triad—Space, Semiconductors and AI—lies in their convergence, underpinned by India’s revolutionary Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), commonly known as the India Stack.
